tx_pilgrims_pride_jizzercise_boulders.blurb: Two small riverside boulders on the Nolan River near Blum, in north-central Texas, holding 14 problems between them. The grades run from V0 up to V5, with the bulk of the problems in the V3 to V4 range, so it suits someone already comfortable on moderate boulders more than a first-timer. Pilgrims Pride is the bigger block and carries only a handful of lines, with a fair amount of dirty rock across its face. Jizzercise is the smaller one, shaped around a blunt fin. You can pick the boulders out from the bridge, and the low ground beside the water means they are sometimes flooded. Expect a short outing rather than a full day.

tx_front_wall_2.blurb: A steep limestone wall in the last canyon on the far side of Miller Springs, on Lake Belton near Belton. It holds 14 routes, almost all of them bolted sport lines plus a single trad line. The difficulty sits high: a couple of 5.10s, then most routes in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, with one a notch above. There are a few easier warm-ups but not many. The wall is steep and roofed, and the rock is rougher than on the neighbouring Wrath Wall, with some loose sections. The bolts date from the early 1990s, so this is a place for experienced hard sport climbers who are happy to check their gear and expect a long walk in.

tx_buda_belly_wall.blurb: The first wall you meet when hiking west along the creek-bed trail into Medicine Wall, on the north side of San Antonio. It is a limestone crag with 14 climbs, mostly bolted sport routes, with top-rope access to some lines and one boulder problem. Grades run from an easy 5.6 through to the low 5.11s, with a good cluster in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, which makes it friendlier than much of Medicine Wall. A bulge about halfway up gives the wall its name and character. The wider cliff area faces north, so it offers some summer shade but feels cold in winter. Loose rock turns up around here, so wear a helmet.
